faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about setting up and running games with PointFinder.

gettingStarted.whatIsA: PointFinder is an NFC-based adventure game platform designed for scouting and youth organizations. Organizers place physical NFC tags at outdoor locations (bases), create challenges for teams to complete, and monitor everything in real time through a web dashboard.
gettingStarted.firstGameQ: How do I create my first game?
gettingStarted.firstGameA: Sign up as an operator, then create a new game from the dashboard. Add bases with GPS coordinates, write challenges (photo, text, or quiz), organize players into teams, and go live when you're ready. The platform guides you through each step with a readiness checklist.
gettingStarted.equipmentA: All you need are NFC tags (inexpensive stickers or cards) and smartphones. Place NFC tags at each base location, and teams use the iOS or Android app to scan them. The web admin panel runs in any browser for game management.

gameSetup.basesA: Bases are physical locations where you place NFC tags. Each base is mapped with GPS coordinates and shown on the interactive map. Teams visit bases in the field and scan the NFC tag to check in and receive their challenge.
gameSetup.challengesA: Challenges are tasks assigned at each base. They can require a text answer (with optional auto-validation), a photo submission for manual review, or a quiz. Each challenge has a point value that contributes to the team's score.
gameSetup.assignmentA: You can assign challenges to bases in two modes: uniform assignment gives every team the same challenge at each base, while random assignment gives each team a different challenge per base. You can also fix specific challenges to specific bases for full control.
gameSetup.variablesA: Team variables are custom placeholders you define in challenge text that get replaced with unique values per team. For example, a challenge might say "Go to {{nextCoordinates}}" where each team receives different coordinates, creating personalized experiences.

playing.joinQ: How do teams join a game?
playing.joinA: Players download the PointFinder app (iOS or Android), enter the game code shared by the organizer, and join their assigned team. They can then see the map with base locations and start exploring.
playing.nfcScanA: When a team arrives at a base, they tap their phone against the NFC tag. The app reads the tag, verifies the base, checks the team in, and reveals their challenge. It works with any NFC-enabled smartphone.
playing.afterScanA: After scanning, the team sees their challenge and submits a response — either a text answer or a photo. Text answers can be auto-validated against correct answers, while photo submissions go to operators for manual review.
playing.offlineA: Yes. Core features like NFC scanning and challenge viewing work without an internet connection. Submissions are queued locally and automatically sync when connectivity is restored.

operator.monitorQ: How do I monitor a live game?
operator.monitorA: The web admin provides a real-time dashboard with a live map showing team positions, a leaderboard with instant score updates, an activity feed of all game events, and a submission review queue.
operator.reviewA: When teams submit photo answers, they appear in the operator's review queue. Operators can approve or reject each submission with optional feedback. Approved submissions award points; rejected ones notify the team to try again.
operator.broadcastQ: Can I broadcast the game publicly?
operator.broadcastA: Yes. Enable broadcast mode in game settings to generate a public link. Spectators can watch the live leaderboard, map, and activity feed without logging in — perfect for projecting at events.
operator.multipleQ: Can multiple people manage a game?
operator.multipleA: Yes. The game owner can invite other operators by email. Invited operators get full access to the game dashboard, submission review, and monitoring tools.

platform.supportedA: PointFinder offers native apps for iOS and Android (for players and operators in the field) and a full-featured web admin dashboard (for game creation, management, and live monitoring).
platform.mapsA: You can choose from several tile providers per game: OpenStreetMap, OpenStreetMap Classic, CartoDB Voyager, CartoDB Positron, and SwissTopo (including satellite view). The map choice applies across all platforms.
platform.languagesA: PointFinder is available in English, Portuguese, and German. The app automatically detects the device language and switches accordingly.

welcome.title: Build your first game, guided
welcome.body: A short walkthrough on a real game of your own. We highlight the next thing to do and explain what each screen offers. Nothing is created for you, and you can stop at any time.

library.title: Tutorials
library.subtitle: Guided walkthroughs on a practice game of your own. Your real games are never touched.
library.loadFailed: We could not load your tutorial progress.

practice.createFailed: We could not set up the practice game.

firstGame.title: Run your first game
firstGame.blurb: From an empty dashboard to a live game and back to setup: bases, challenges, teams, assignments and go-live.

fixedRoute.title: Make a fixed route
fixedRoute.blurb: Bases unlock one at a time in an order you arrange, so every team follows the same path.

exploration.title: Hide bases for exploration
exploration.blurb: Keep bases off the player map until a team finds them, and use completion text to hand out the clues.

unlockChain.title: Chain the unlocks
unlockChain.blurb: One base leads to the next, a fork lets teams choose, and a bonus base hides back down the trail.

differentPath.title: A different path
differentPath.blurb: Two teams, the same three bases and challenges in the same order, but starting from opposite ends.

variableOutcome.title: A variable outcome
variableOutcome.blurb: One completion text that sends each team somewhere different, through a team variable.

create-game.title: Start with a game
create-game.body: Every event lives inside a game, and a new game always begins in setup. Tap New Game to start one — renaming, dates and importing a finished game all live on this screen too.

name-game.title: Name it and create it
name-game.body: Name it after the event; the description is optional and can wait. Create opens the game in its workspace, still in setup.

orient.title: Your readiness checklist
orient.body: The map is your canvas: bases sit on it and everything else hangs off them. This pill counts what is still missing before the game can go live. Open it any time for the full list.
orient.aside: It only appears while the game is in setup.

place-base.title: Place your first base
place-base.body: Tap the map where players should go, then choose Place base here. You can drag the marker later to move it, or add bases from the content panel if you would rather type coordinates.

base-name.title: Name the base
base-name.body: Players see this name on their map and in their list, so name it after the place: "Old mill", "Chapel steps". It is prefilled — change it to something a stranger could find.

base-description.title: Describe it (optional)
base-description.body: A sentence of context for players — what the spot looks like, where to stand. Leave it empty when the name is enough on its own.

base-coords.title: Check the coordinates
base-coords.body: These came from where you tapped. Drag the marker on the small map to adjust them, or type exact values if you already have them from a survey.

base-method.title: How players check in
base-method.body: Tap how a team proves it arrived: an NFC tag you write, a QR code you print, or GPS location. The current choice is highlighted — tap one to confirm it. The game-wide default lives in settings.

base-radius.title: Set the GPS radius
base-radius.body: Location bases unlock inside this ring. Too small and phones with poor accuracy struggle; too large and neighbouring bases overlap. The readiness list warns you when two rings touch. The inherited game default is a fine starting point — press Next to keep it.
base-radius.aside: Leave it empty to inherit the game default.

base-visibility.title: Visible or hidden
base-visibility.body: Visible bases show on the player map from the start. Hidden ones stay off it until a team finds them — the basis of exploration games, which have their own tutorial.

base-link.title: Pin one challenge
base-link.body: A base can hold one fixed challenge, so the same task always waits there. You have no challenges yet — assignments come later and can differ per team.

base-save.title: Save the base
base-save.body: Save writes the base to the server. Nothing is live yet: teams see none of this until you go live, so edit as freely as you like.

base-qr.title: Print the QR code
base-qr.body: This base unlocks by QR code. Print it and put it at the location, weatherproofed if it lives outdoors. The Tags & codes tab prints every code on one sheet. Close the print sheet when you are done.

base-nfc.title: Write the NFC tag
base-nfc.body: This base needs a tag written to it. Hold a blank NFC tag against the phone and write it. No tag with you right now? Do it later — the Tags tab lists every unlinked base.
base-nfc.aside: On a computer, open the Tags & codes tab and write the tag from the phone app.

second-base.title: Add a second base
second-base.body: One base is not a route. Place another far enough away that the two do not overlap, then save it. Later bases skip this field-by-field walkthrough.

new-challenge.title: Create a challenge
new-challenge.body: Challenges are the tasks teams answer. The content panel holds bases, challenges, teams, stages, and tags & codes — New adds one to whichever tab you are on.

challenge-title.title: Title the challenge
challenge-title.body: This is what players see in their list before they open it, so keep it short and concrete. It is prefilled — replace it. Required.

challenge-type.title: Choose an answer type
challenge-type.body: Text for a typed answer, File for a photo or recording, None when reaching the base is the whole task. Text is preselected.

challenge-content.title: Write the task
challenge-content.body: This is the challenge itself, shown once a team unlocks it. Formatting, embedded files and per-team variables all work, so one challenge can hand each team a different clue.

challenge-description.title: Short summary (optional)
challenge-description.body: One line shown in lists next to the title. Handy when several challenges look alike; skip it otherwise.

challenge-autovalidate.title: Who checks the answer
challenge-autovalidate.body: On, the app compares the answer to the one you set and accepts it instantly. Off, the submission waits for you in Review mode — which is what file answers need.

challenge-answer.title: Set the correct answer
challenge-answer.body: Auto-validate needs something to compare against. Matching ignores capitals and surrounding spaces, so type the answer the way a player would write it.

challenge-points.title: Points
challenge-points.body: The scoring weight of this challenge. Players never see points or a leaderboard — scoring is yours alone, in Results mode.

challenge-completion.title: After they finish
challenge-completion.body: Optional text shown to the team the moment this challenge is done. Good for a thank-you, the next hint, or the clue to a hidden base.

challenge-location-bound.title: Require being there
challenge-location-bound.body: On, the challenge can only be answered at its base. Off, a team can answer from anywhere once it is unlocked — useful for research or photo tasks.

challenge-notes.title: Notes for your team
challenge-notes.body: Private notes for you and your fellow operators: the expected answer, safety warnings, who looks after this base. Players never receive this field.

challenge-save.title: Save the challenge
challenge-save.body: Save it. Everything above stays editable while the game is in setup, and most of it stays editable while the game is running.

more-challenges.title: One per base
more-challenges.body: Add challenges until every base has at least one. Duplicating your first one and editing it is usually faster than starting from scratch.

assign.title: Link challenges to bases
assign.body: Assignments decide which challenge waits at which base. Auto-assign pairs each base that has nothing yet with an unused challenge, in order; open a base to pick by hand, or open Assignments for a different route per team.

new-team.title: Create a team
new-team.body: Players never join alone — they join a team. Create one now; you can add more, rename them, recolour them and set team variables at any time.

team-code.title: The join code
team-code.body: Players type this code in the app to join, or scan the QR beside it. Codes stay valid for the whole game, so you can print them on a handout.

go-live.title: Go live
go-live.body: Every check has passed. Going live fixes the route, hands the challenges to the teams and opens check-ins. You can come back to setup afterwards.

branch.nfcPending: One NFC base still has no tag written, and that is the only thing left. Write it from the Tags & codes tab, or switch that base to a QR code or GPS instead.
branch.notReady: Some checks are still red. Open the checklist to see which — usually a base with no challenge, a missing team, or an NFC tag that has not been written yet.

modes.title: The four modes
modes.body: Build is where you have been. Command watches teams live on the map, Review handles submissions waiting for you, and Results holds scoring and the export.

revert.title: Back to setup
revert.body: Need a change after going live? Back to setup reopens the game for editing. Tap it — the next question is what to do with the progress so far.

revert-choice.title: Keep or erase progress
revert-choice.body: Keep keeps every check-in and submission so teams carry on where they were; erase starts the event over. History is archived either way. Choose, then confirm.

edit.title: Edit anything
edit.body: In setup everything is editable again. Open the first challenge to change it.

edit-location-bound.title: Make it location bound
edit-location-bound.body: Location bound means the challenge can only be answered at its base, not from anywhere once unlocked. Turn it on for this one.

edit-save.title: Save the change
edit-save.body: Save. The change waits in setup until you go live again.

go-live-again.title: Go live again
go-live-again.body: Reopen the game. Teams pick up where they left off if you kept progress, or start clean if you erased it.

finish.title: That is your first game
finish.body: You built a game, ran it, changed it and ran it again. Two more tutorials cover fixed routes, where bases unlock one at a time, and exploration games with hidden bases. This is a practice game: keep it as your real game, or delete it.

enable-order.title: Turn on the route
enable-order.body: Switch on Enforce base order. Teams then check in at bases in one shared order: base 2 is refused until base 1 is done. This panel also holds the game name, map style, operators and export.

unlock-trigger.title: What unlocks the next base
unlock-trigger.body: Check-in can be enough, or you can require a submission or an approved answer. The setting covers the whole game, not just the route. For a first route, check-in keeps teams moving.

add-bases.title: Add a second base
add-bases.body: A route needs at least two bases, and Arrange route stays disabled until then. Add one more with New Base — the tour moves on as soon as it exists.

arrange.title: Open the route editor
arrange.body: Arrange route opens the running order. It needs at least two bases and only works while the game is in setup. Beside it are the search, the base list and every base you can edit.

route.title: Set the order
route.body: Drag a base or use the arrows, then save. Every base already has a number, so the route is never incomplete — you only choose who comes first. One route serves all teams; challenges can still differ.

readiness.title: Before you go live
readiness.body: The route itself has no check here: every base is numbered automatically. This pill still guards bases, challenges, teams, assignments and check-in methods. Expand it any time to see what is missing.

finish.title: Route done
finish.body: Bases now unlock in order. Keep this practice game or delete it — your own games were not touched.

place-first.title: Place a base first
place-first.body: This game has no bases yet. Tap the map where players should end up and choose Place base here. The map is also where you drag markers and open a base for editing.

pick-base.title: Pick a base to hide
pick-base.body: Open a base from this list. Everything about it lives in the panel that opens: name, coordinates, check-in method, tags and visibility. Search filters the list once a game grows.

hide.title: Hide it from the map
hide.body: Choose Hidden. Players get no pin and no list row for this base until they check in there. A hidden GPS base still fires when a team walks into its radius.

hide-save.title: Save the base
hide-save.body: Visibility is a draft until you save. Saving writes it and the list shows a Hidden tag. Nothing else on this form changes — you can keep editing the base afterwards.

clue.title: Write the clue
clue.body: Unlocked Information is what a team reads after finishing a challenge. Put the clue to the hidden base here: a landmark, a riddle, a bearing. There is no pin to follow, so this text is the only guide.

readiness.title: Hidden bases still count
readiness.body: Readiness treats a hidden base like any other: it needs a working check-in method, and an NFC one needs a linked tag. Expand the pill for the full checklist before going live.

finish.title: Hidden and clued
finish.body: Players will find that base from the clue, not the map. Keep this practice game or delete it — your own games were not touched.

practice.kept: This is now a normal game.
practice.settingsBody: A tutorial created this game. It takes one player and ends itself in {{hours}} h. Keep it to turn it into a normal game, or delete it.
practice.settingsBodyEnded: A tutorial created this game and it has ended. Keep it to turn it into a normal game, or delete it.

intro.title: Only the trailhead shows
intro.body: Five bases are hidden. Each appears when a team completes the challenge that reveals it: the bridge, then a fork, then a bonus back down the trail or the summit. The first link is missing — you will set it.

open-first.title: Open the trailhead challenge
open-first.body: Reveals are set on the challenge that is pinned to a base and location bound. Open the trailhead's challenge.

reveal.title: Reveal the old bridge
reveal.body: Under Reveals bases, pick Old bridge. When a team completes this challenge at the trailhead, the bridge appears on their map.

save-reveal.title: Save the link
save-reveal.body: Save. The chain now runs from the trailhead.

fork.title: A fork
fork.body: The bridge's challenge reveals two bases at once: the tower and the ford. Teams choose which to go for — both count.

bonus.title: A bonus behind them
bonus.body: The tower's challenge reveals a cache back down the trail; the ford's reveals the summit. Going back is a team decision worth points.

finish.title: Chain done
finish.body: Bases that appear one by one make a route feel like a discovery. Keep this practice game or delete it.

intro.title: Same bases, opposite starts
intro.body: Three bases in a triangle, three challenges. Falcons start at A and end at C; Lions start at C and end at A. Both do challenge 1 first, then 2, then 3 — so what changes is which base carries which challenge for each team.

open-grid.title: Open Assignments
open-grid.body: Assignments is the grid: rows are bases, one column per team. Open it.

falcons.title: Falcons: A→1, B→2, C→3
falcons.body: In the Falcons column, give base A challenge 1, base B challenge 2 and base C challenge 3.

lions.title: Lions: C→1, B→2, A→3
lions.body: In the Lions column, base C gets challenge 1, base B challenge 2, base A challenge 3. The grid keeps a challenge at one base per team, so the two columns can differ freely.

briefing.title: Tell them where to start
briefing.body: Nothing enforces a physical order here; each team simply starts where you send them. Put the start in the team's briefing, or use a fixed route when order must be enforced.

finish.title: Two paths, one game
finish.body: That is how one set of bases serves opposite routes. Keep this practice game or delete it.

intro.title: Same words, different destination
intro.body: After the old mill, Falcons should be sent to the chapel and Lions to the lookout — with one completion text. Team variables do that: write {{next}} once, give each team its own value.

open-challenge.title: Open the pinned challenge
open-challenge.body: The old mill's challenge is pinned to its base. Open it.

variable-key.title: Name the variable
variable-key.body: Under Challenge variables, type the key: next.

variable-add.title: Add it
variable-add.body: Add the variable. A value field appears for every team.

variable-values.title: One value per team
variable-values.body: Give Falcons the chapel and Lions the lookout. Every team needs a value before the game can go live.

completion.title: Use it in the completion text
completion.body: In the post-completion text, type {{next}} where the destination goes, e.g. "Good work — go to {{next}}." The preview resolves it per team.

challenge-save.title: Save the challenge
challenge-save.body: Save. Each team now reads its own next stop.

finish.title: Variable done
finish.body: Variables work anywhere in a challenge's text or answer. Keep this practice game or delete it.

introduction.title: How PointFinder works
introduction.blurb: The one-minute introduction: planning, bases, challenges, teams, going live and results.

transfer.title: Transfer ownership
transfer.desc: The new owner must already be a member, and is granted every permission.
transfer.confirm: Hand {{club}} to {{name}}? They gain every permission over the club.
transfer.noCandidates: There is no other member to hand the club to.
transfer.creatorDesc: You created this club, so you cannot leave it. Hand it to another member first.

leave.title: Leave this club
leave.desc: You lose access to the club’s games and resources. Your personal workspace is untouched.
leave.confirm: Leave "{{name}}"? You lose access to its games and resources, and would need a new invitation to come back.
